literal: " Changgong said, "How could the emperor's face ever be seen?
idiomatic: Changgong said, "How could I ever look upon the emperor's face?"

literal: " He then drank the poison and died.
idiomatic: He drank the poison and died.

literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand commandant.

literal: Changgong's face was gentle but his heart was bold; voice and bearing alike were beautiful.
idiomatic: Changgong looked gentle but his heart was bold; in voice and bearing alike he was beautiful.

literal: As a general he personally attended to the smallest matters; whenever he obtained anything sweet or fine, even a single melon or a few fruits, he always shared them with his officers and men.
idiomatic: As a general he personally saw to the smallest things; whenever he had anything sweet or fine — even a melon or a few fruits — he shared it with his officers and men.

literal: At first, while in Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shibiao submitted a detailed list of his corrupt acts, and he was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: While governor of Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shibiao submitted a detailed list of his corruption, and he was dismissed.

literal: When they campaigned against Dingyang, Shi Shen was with the army [5], fearing that retribution would reach him.
idiomatic: During the campaign against Dingyang, Shi Shen was with the army [5] and feared retribution.

literal: Changgong heard of it and said, "I never had such an intention.
idiomatic: Changgong heard and said, "That was never my intent.

literal: " He then found a minor fault, had Shi Shen beaten twenty strokes, and so reassured him.
idiomatic: " He then found a minor fault, had Shi Shen beaten twenty strokes, and put the matter to rest.

literal: Once when he went to court his attendants all scattered, and only one remained; Changgong returned alone without punishing anyone.
idiomatic: Once on his way to court his attendants all fled save one; Changgong returned alone and punished no one.

literal: Wucheng rewarded his achievements and ordered Jia Hu to buy twenty concubines for him; he accepted only one.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan rewarded his service and ordered Jia Hu to buy him twenty concubines; he accepted only one.

literal: He held promissory notes worth a thousand gold; on the day he died, he burned them all.
idiomatic: He held promissory notes worth a thousand gold; on the day of his death he burned them all.

literal: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Wenxiang.
idiomatic: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Gao Cheng.

literal: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan of the Prince of Guangyang.
idiomatic: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan of the Prince of Guangyang.

literal: Yanzong was raised from childhood by Wenxuan; even at twelve Wenxuan would set him astride his belly, make him urinate into his navel, hold him close and say, "Pitiful — I have only this one.
idiomatic: Yanzong was raised from childhood by Gao Yang; even at twelve the emperor would set him astride his belly, make him urinate into his navel, hold him close and say, "Poor child — I have only this one.

literal: " He asked what prince Yanzong wished to be; the boy answered, "I wish to be Prince Storm-the-Heavens.
idiomatic: " He asked what title the boy wanted; Yanzong answered, "I want to be Prince Heaven-Storm.

literal: " Wenxuan asked Yang Yin; Yang said, "There is no such commandery in the realm — I wish he may dwell secure in virtue.
idiomatic: " Gao Yang asked Yang Yin; Yang said, "No such commandery exists in the realm — let him dwell secure in virtue instead.

literal: " And so he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.
idiomatic: " And so he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande.

literal: As governor of Ding Province, he would defecate from an upper story, having men below open their mouths to catch it.
idiomatic: As governor of Ding Province he would defecate from an upper story while men below opened their mouths to receive it.

literal: He mixed steamed grain with human dung to feed his attendants, and whipped any who showed revulsion.
idiomatic: He mixed steamed grain with human dung to feed his attendants and whipped any who looked disgusted.

literal: Emperor Xiaozhao heard of it and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him a hundred strokes.
idiomatic: Emperor Gao Yan heard and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him a hundred strokes.

literal: Daode, seeing that Yanzong did not take the beating with proper deference, added thirty more.
idiomatic: Daode, finding Yanzong insufficiently deferential under the rod, added thirty strokes.

literal: He also tested blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.
idiomatic: He also tested blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.

literal: Arrogant and unrestrained, he committed many unlawful acts.
idiomatic: Arrogant and unrestrained, he broke the law in many ways.

literal: Wucheng had him flogged and killed nine of his closest intimates; from this Yanzong deeply repented.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan had him flogged and killed nine of his closest intimates; from that Yanzong deeply repented.

literal: When Prince Changgong of Lanling reported his victory at Mangshan and described his military strength, all the brothers praised him.
idiomatic: When Prince Changgong of Lanling reported his victory at Mangshan and described his forces, all his brothers praised him.

literal: Yanzong alone said, "Fourth brother is no true man — why did he not press the advantage and march straight in?
idiomatic: Yanzong alone said, "Fourth brother is no true man — why not press the victory and march straight in?"

literal: If Yanzong were in that position, how could the lands west of the passes still stand?
idiomatic: Had Yanzong held that position, how could the lands west of the passes still stand?

literal: " When Changgong of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng offered her neck-pearl to the Buddha.
idiomatic: When Changgong of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng offered her neck-pearl to the Buddha.

literal: The Prince of Guangning sent men to redeem it.
idiomatic: The Prince of Guangning sent men to redeem it.

literal: Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, tears flooding the page.
idiomatic: Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, the page soaked with tears.

literal: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong wept for him with equal grief.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong wept for him with equal grief.

literal: He also made a straw effigy in Wucheng's likeness, whipped it and interrogated it: "Why did you kill my brother!
idiomatic: He also made a straw effigy in Gao Zhan's likeness, whipped it and demanded, "Why did you kill my brother!"

literal: " A servant reported it; Wucheng had Yanzong thrown face-down to the ground and lashed two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.
idiomatic: A servant reported it; Gao Zhan had Yanzong thrown face-down and lashed two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.

literal: Later he served successively as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Later he served as minister over the masses and grand commandant.

literal: At the battle of Pingyang, Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first engagement; below the walls they captured Zhou's general Zong Ting.
idiomatic: At Pingyang Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first attack; below the walls they captured Zhou general Zong Ting.

literal: In the great battle, Yanzong with his troops charged twice into the Zhou army, and none could stand before them.
idiomatic: In the great battle Yanzong led his men twice into the Zhou army, and none could stand before them.

literal: The other armies were defeated; Yanzong alone kept his force intact.
idiomatic: The other armies broke; Yanzong alone kept his force intact.

literal: As Houzhu was about to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only remain in camp without moving; give me command of the cavalry and infantry and I can break them.
idiomatic: As Houzhu prepared to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only stay in camp; give me the army and I can break them.

literal: " The emperor would not accept this.
idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

literal: When they reached Bing Province and heard that Zhou troops had entered Queyu Valley [6], he made Yanzong Chancellor and governor of Bing Province, putting him in overall charge of military affairs west of the mountains.
idiomatic: At Bing Province, hearing Zhou troops had entered Queyu Valley [6], he made Yanzong chancellor and governor of Bing Province, giving him overall command of military affairs west of the mountains.

literal: He said to him, "Bing Province — elder brother takes it for himself; your son departs now.
idiomatic: He told him, "Bing Province — elder brother takes it for himself; your son leaves now.

literal: " Yanzong said, "Your Majesty must not move for the sake of the altars of state; your servant will fight to the death for Your Majesty.
idiomatic: " Yanzong said, "Your Majesty must not stir for the altars of state; your servant will fight to the death for you.

literal: " Luotipo said, "His Majesty's plan is already set — the prince must not obstruct it.
idiomatic: " Luotipo said, "His Majesty's plan is set — the prince must not obstruct it.

literal: " Houzhu fled to Ye after all.
idiomatic: Houzhu fled to Ye after all.

literal: The commanders at Bing all petitioned: "If the prince will not become Son of Heaven, we truly cannot fight to the death.
idiomatic: The commanders at Bing all petitioned: "If the prince will not become emperor, we truly cannot fight to the death.

literal: " Yanzong had no choice but to take the imperial throne, and issued an edict: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay in the hands of eunuchs; strife arose within the palace walls, and invaders rose on the borders.
idiomatic: " Yanzong had no choice but to take the throne and issued an edict: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay with eunuchs; strife rose within the palace walls and invaders on the borders.

literal: He who should hold the passes fled by night with none knowing whither — and our Gaozu's enterprise was about to crash to earth.
idiomatic: He who should hold the passes fled by night, none knew where — and our founder's enterprise was about to crash to earth.

literal: Lords and ministers, though unworthy, have pressed me; I now reverently assume the sacred throne.
idiomatic: Lords and ministers, though unworthy, have pressed me; I now reverently take the throne.

literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm; change the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang.
idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty; change the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang.

literal: " He appointed Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang as chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang [7]; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; General of Opening Gates Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou as his strong arms.
idiomatic: " He made Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang [7]; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; opening-gates general Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou his strong arms.

literal: When the multitudes heard, those who came without being summoned followed one after another.
idiomatic: When word spread, men came unbidden in endless succession.

literal: Yanzong was full and sturdy of build; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled flat — people laughed at him until he suddenly blazed into action.
idiomatic: Yanzong was full and sturdy of build; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled — people laughed until he suddenly blazed into action.

literal: His strength was beyond compare; charging through battle lines he was swift and fierce as flight itself.
idiomatic: His strength was beyond compare; charging through battle lines he was swift and fierce as flight.

literal: He emptied the treasury and the palace beauties to reward the troops, and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.
idiomatic: He emptied the treasury and the palace women to reward the troops and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.

literal: Houzhu told his close attendants, "I would rather let Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it.
idiomatic: Houzhu told his close attendants, "I would rather Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it.

literal: " Those beside him said, "That is only reasonable.
idiomatic: " Those beside him said, "That is only reasonable.

literal: " When Yanzong met the soldiers he personally grasped each man's hand, spoke his own name in clear words, weeping and choking with sobs.
idiomatic: " When Yanzong met the soldiers he grasped each man's hand, spoke his own name, weeping and choking with sobs.

literal: All competed to die for him; boys and girls too climbed rooftops, baring their sleeves, and hurled wax-stones at the Zhou army.
idiomatic: All competed to die for him; boys and girls too climbed rooftops, baring their sleeves, and hurled wax-stones at the Zhou army.

literal: Special Advance and General of Opening Gates Nalu Ansheng held Taigu with ten thousand men and rebelled.
idiomatic: Special advance and opening-gates general Nalu Ansheng held Taigu with ten thousand men and rebelled.

literal: Zhou troops besieged Jinyang; seen from afar they were like black clouds closing on every side.
idiomatic: Zhou troops besieged Jinyang; seen from afar they were like black clouds closing on every side.

literal: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall, and Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang the east.
idiomatic: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall, and Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang the east.

literal: Yanzong personally faced Zhou's Prince of Qi at the north wall, wielding a great spear, riding back and forth to direct the fight — nowhere was there resistance before him.
idiomatic: Yanzong personally faced Zhou's Prince of Qi at the north wall, wielding a great spear, riding back and forth to direct the fight — nowhere could anyone stand before him.

literal: The Records Clerk of the Masters of Writing, Ju Shan, also fat and immensely strong, followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.
idiomatic: Ju Shan, records clerk of the Masters of Writing, also fat and immensely strong, followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.

literal: Martial Guard Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in battle.
idiomatic: Martial Guard Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in battle.

literal: Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang defected to Zhou with a thousand horsemen.
idiomatic: Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang defected to Zhou with a thousand horsemen.

literal: Zhou troops assaulted the east gate; at dusk they broke through.
idiomatic: Zhou troops assaulted the east gate; at dusk they broke through.

literal: They advanced, burning the gate and hall of the Buddhist temple; soaring flames lit heaven and earth.
idiomatic: They advanced, burning the gate and hall of the Buddhist temple; soaring flames lit heaven and earth.

literal: Yanzong and Jingxian entered from the gate and struck from both sides; the Zhou army fell into chaos, men crowding the gate and crushing one another; Qi troops hacked and stabbed from behind — more than two thousand dead.
idiomatic: Yanzong and Jingxian entered from the gate and struck from both sides; the Zhou army fell into chaos, men crowding the gate and crushing one another; Qi troops hacked and stabbed from behind — more than two thousand dead.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou's attendants were nearly all gone; he could not extricate himself and had no way out. Senior Attendant Zhang Shou seized the bridle, and Helu Fo'en lashed from behind — over broken ground they barely escaped.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou's attendants were nearly all gone; he could not extricate himself. Senior attendant Zhang Shou seized the bridle, Helu Fo'en lashed from behind — over broken ground they barely escaped.

literal: Qi troops pressed the attack and nearly struck him down.
idiomatic: Qi troops pressed the attack and nearly struck him down.

literal: East of the wall the paths twisted narrow; Fo'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely survived — it was the fourth watch of the night.
idiomatic: East of the wall the paths twisted narrow; Fo'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely survived — it was the fourth watch.

literal: Yanzong believed Emperor Wu of Zhou had fallen in the turmoil and had men search the heaped corpses for a man with long whiskers; they did not find one.
idiomatic: Yanzong believed Emperor Wu of Zhou had fallen in the turmoil and had men search the heaped corpses for a man with long whiskers; they found none.

literal: By then the Qi men, victorious, went into the wards to drink, all drunk and fallen asleep — Yanzong could no longer restore order.
idiomatic: By then the Qi men, victorious, went into the wards to drink until all were drunk and asleep — Yanzong could no longer restore order.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou left the city, racked with hunger, and intended a plan of flight.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou left the city, racked with hunger, and planned to flee.

literal: Prince Xian of Qi and Pillar of State Wang Yi remonstrated, saying that if he left he would surely not escape.
idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi and pillar of state Wang Yi remonstrated, saying that if he left he would surely not escape.

literal: Yanzong's defecting general Duan Chang also loudly declared that the city was empty within.
idiomatic: Yanzong's defecting general Duan Chang also loudly declared the city empty within.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou then halted his horse, sounded the horn to recall his troops, and in a moment rallied again.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou halted his horse, sounded the horn to recall his troops, and in a moment rallied again.

literal: At dawn they again attacked the east gate, took it, and entered the south gate as well.
idiomatic: At dawn they attacked the east gate again, took it, and entered the south gate as well.

literal: Yanzong fought until his strength gave out, fled to the north of the city, and was captured in a common household.
idiomatic: Yanzong fought until his strength gave out, fled to the north of the city, and was captured in a commoner's house.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou himself dismounted and took his hand.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou himself dismounted and took his hand.

literal: Yanzong declined: "The hand of a dead man — how dare it touch His Majesty.
idiomatic: Yanzong declined: "The hand of a dead man — how dare it touch Your Majesty.

literal: " The emperor said, "Two realm-sovereigns — what hatred between us? I came only for the people.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Two sovereigns — what hatred between us? I came only for the people.

literal: Do not fear; in the end I will not harm you.
idiomatic: Do not fear; in the end I will not harm you.

literal: " He had Yanzong restored to cap and robes and treated him with courtesy.
idiomatic: " He had Yanzong restored to cap and robes and treated him with courtesy.

literal: Before this, in Gaodu Commandery there was a mountain with sheer cliffs over water; suddenly black writing appeared, reading "Qi falls — Yanzong"; washed, it grew clearer still.
idiomatic: Before this, in Gaodu Commandery there was a mountain with sheer cliffs over water; suddenly black writing appeared: "Qi falls — Yanzong"; washed, it grew clearer still.

literal: The emperor sent men to copy it; the envoy changed "falls" to "rises."
idiomatic: The emperor sent men to copy it; the envoy changed "falls" to "rises."

literal: Now it was fulfilled.
idiomatic: Now it was fulfilled.

literal: Before Yanzong's defeat, at the hall in Ye he saw two suns placed one above the other; on the thirteenth of the twelfth month in the afternoon watch he received orders to hold Bing Province; the next day he took the imperial title; without a day's interval he was besieged; one night passed, and by mealtime he was defeated.
idiomatic: Before Yanzong's defeat, at the hall in Ye he saw two suns placed one above the other; on the thirteenth of the twelfth month in the afternoon watch he received orders to hold Bing Province; the next day he took the throne; without a day's interval he was besieged; one night passed, and by mealtime he was defeated.

literal: The era name was Dechang — gossips said he had gotten his "two suns."
idiomatic: The era name was Dechang — gossips said he had gotten his "two suns."

literal: Soon after, Emperor Wu of Zhou asked for a plan to take Ye.
idiomatic: Soon after, Emperor Wu of Zhou asked for a plan to take Ye.

literal: He declined: "A minister of a fallen state cannot plot survival — this is beyond me.
idiomatic: He declined: "A minister of a fallen state cannot plot survival — this is beyond me.

literal: " Pressed hard, he finally said, "If the Prince of Rencheng comes to relieve Ye, I cannot say; if the present sovereign holds it himself, Your Majesty's army need not draw blood."
idiomatic: " Pressed hard, he finally said, "If the Prince of Rencheng comes to relieve Ye, I cannot say; if the present sovereign holds it himself, Your Majesty's army need not draw blood."

literal: When they reached Chang'an, Emperor Wu of Zhou drank with the Qi lords and ministers, ordering Houzhu to dance; Yanzong's grief was beyond his control.
idiomatic: At Chang'an Emperor Wu of Zhou drank with the Qi lords and ministers, ordering Houzhu to dance; Yanzong's grief was beyond his control.

literal: Repeatedly he wished to raise poison and kill himself; his serving women clung to him and remonstrated until he stopped.
idiomatic: Repeatedly he wished to take poison and kill himself; his serving women clung to him and remonstrated until he stopped.

literal: Before long Emperor Wu of Zhou falsely charged Houzhu and Yanzong and the rest with remotely responding to Mutipo's rebellion and ordered them all put to death by edict.
idiomatic: Before long Emperor Wu of Zhou falsely charged Houzhu, Yanzong, and the rest with remotely responding to Mutipo's rebellion and ordered them all put to death.

literal: All protested their innocence; Yanzong rolled up his sleeves, wept, and said nothing.
idiomatic: All protested their innocence; Yanzong rolled up his sleeves, wept, and said nothing.

literal: All were killed with pepper stuffed in their mouths.
idiomatic: All were killed with pepper stuffed in their mouths.

literal: The next year Consort Li gathered their remains for burial.
idiomatic: The next year Consort Li gathered their remains for burial.

literal: Footnote marker eight in the source.
idiomatic: Footnote 8 in the source text.
